newsitem.title: UK: Write-off sparks Shell Q3 disappointment.
newsitem.headline: Write-off sparks Shell Q3 disappointment.

text.p: An unusually high exploration write-off was the main reason why third quarter earnings for Royal Dutch/Shell Group came in at the low end of market forecasts, analysts said on Thursday.
But they added the write-off gave no cause for any concern.
"It is a mere random event and has nothing to do what actually happens in the quarter," said Nick Antill at BZW.
Analyst had expected earnings of around 1.206 billion stg, while they actually came in at 1.117 billion.
"The reason for that was almost entirely a higher than usual exploration write-off," Antill said.
Royal Dutch/Shell reported a surge in exploration and production results, but said downstream marketing and refining earnings suffered from higher costs.
Trading conditions in the chemicals sector had remained difficult, the Anglo-Dutch oil giant said.
Antill said he was worried by the firm's flat capital expenditure, while the company was targeting 25 to 30 percent growth.
Capital expenditure was 1.736 billion stg compared with 1.781 billion in 1995' third quarter. Antill predicted this would prompt an analyst debate over Shell's free cash flow.
"Half of the analyst community will say: 'Isn't it wonderful; the company is very cash generative,' while the other will say it is not investing enough to guarantee growth," Antill said.
He counted himself in the latter camp. "The company is spending less than it needs to spend to go forward," Antill said.
